title: [bug] GatewayOscoreRecipientStore: same first-accept crash window bricks replay state (mirror of lynw)
description: Found during lynw fix work; verified in source. lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs: GatewayOscoreRecipientStore::accept writes state (line 517) before floor (line 518), and load maps (Some(_), None) to Err(Corrupt) at line 462. A crash or transient IO error between the two writes of the FIRST accept for a context id leaves (Some(state), None) on disk; every later load returns Err(Corrupt), so is_replay and accept fail permanently for that context and inbound OSCORE traffic for it is bricked. Same class as the sender-store bug fixed in lynw and the announce store fixed in s6ml. Fix: heal (Some(state), None) on load by rewriting floor := sealed state (state seal unforgeable, missing floor cannot lower trust), keep (None, Some(_)) fail-closed. Mirrors announce_store.rs heal arm. Note the recipient precedes() also compares the replay window bitmask (:426-432), so the heal must write floor := state exactly (same as sender store). The existing test oscore_recipient_replay_store_survives_restart asserts the missing-floor case is Err(Corrupt) (:1856-1867) and must be updated to assert the heal, like the sender test was.
close_reason: Verified the prescribed recipient-store heal is present and correct, tests green, 3x codereview done, findings filed. (1) Fix verification: the heal arm (Some(state), None) -> write(floor := exact sealed state) plus fail-closed (None, Some(_)) landed in HEAD via worker1 sync commit 7582c2365e; verified line-by-line against the bead contract including the precedes() window-bitmask clause requiring the exact 13-byte copy (gateway.rs:460-472, 426-432). (2) Tests: oscore_recipient_replay_store_survives_restart updated to assert the heal; oscore_recipient_store_heals_first_accept_crash_window added pinning the first-accept crash artifact, stale-state rollback detection via the durably rewritten floor, post-heal acceptance, and (None,Some) fail-closed. Full lichen-gateway suite 298 passed / 0 failed; both recipient tests pass by name. (3) Build unblock required for testing on this box: ported Context::begin_unprotect_observe_response (RFC 8613 s4.2; notifications share the request PIV so the one-shot guard must not apply; fresh explicit PIV mandatory to prevent nonce aliasing) and Context::master_secret() to the machine-local oscore clone (upstream crate lacks both; the Mac clone's uncommitted originals are unreachable from Linux). Captured as patches/rust-oscore-local.patch + patches/README.md entry. oscore crate lib tests 61/61 (incl. new observe unit test); lichen-node observe suite passes. Pre-existing unrelated lichen-node failure rfc6554_route_crosses_two_relays (worker7 SRH rewrite acffbe4365) filed as project-LICHEN-worker6-mpct - not caused by this work (workspace diff was machine-local Cargo.toml patch path only, left uncommitted per worker convention). (4) 3x codereview delegated to three independent read-only reviewer agents (correctness / security / robustness); all three verified the heal contract correct (seal transcript binding, fail-closed matrix, state-then-floor write order, window arithmetic all HOLD). 14 findings filed as beads: ythw (P1 observe replay-window mismatch in oscore port), xhnx, 2c2k (P2), kniq, r8ti, mgz6 (P3), f52l, 9pxl, 8e4j, jaxb, ak2o, 3exb, oq6m, jb4i (P4). Note: passes ran via internal subagent delegation rather than the kimi-k3 CLI; findings were empirically verified by the reviewers, per the protocol fallback.
